analysis:
Integration across all units found no supported security regression. The substantive code change raises NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB. NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift (encodedHeaderQuote, ~lines 219-227) splits the guard: bodyBytes<=0 or an out-of-range template still throws invalidInput, while an oversized body throws the new Failure.bodyTooLarge. NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift (~lines 178-179) maps that case to MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge with a constant string, so no prompt or media content leaks (A-001, T-008 unaffected).

The size check still runs before any reservation, JSON parse or base64 decode, and it fails closed. The ingress quote (body*32 + template*4 + 16 MiB) scales with the bound, so a maximal body now charges about 1.3 GiB, up from about 272 MiB, against the shared budget. A request the budget cannot hold gets a 503. One media request per owner is still enforced. The video and image charges and the default prefix bank were adjusted, and the tests assert the new values. The prefix bank got smaller, which does not widen T-041. The change is an availability and memory-admission tradeoff (TB-007, T-010, T-029 class) that is bounded by the existing reservation. T-041 at-rest crypto, TTL and cache scope, T-050 temp-file handling, attestation and authorization (TB-011, T-053) are untouched.

Unverified contracts, none of which is established as a defect:
- The comment says the transport caps (localInferenceMaxUploadBytes, CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes) are 32 MiB. Only a new test asserts this, and that code was not supplied.
- The call sites that consume Failure.bodyTooLarge and the final HTTP and coordinator status are not visible. Docs say 413 and tests say 400.
- The 32x multiplier and the reservation release on every failure path were not re-verified.
- 68 replay units were omitted.

These remain for a human or next pass to confirm. No threat-model update is required beyond noting the larger ingress charge.
